subject: Webcast metric drift — lead assignment & revenue delta
messages:
From: Sophie Liu <sophie@acmemarketing.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Ng <aaron@brightwebinars.io>, hs-sync@acme.com
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Discrepancy in webcast lead counts / revenue attribution

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the webcast last week — we had great attendance. A quick ask: our RevOps team is seeing ~42 leads from the session attributed to Acme’s UT campaign in our HubSpot export, but BrightWebinar is reporting 28 uniques and Redwood’s post-event CSV shows 35. The resulting revenue delta is material for our MRR math this quarter.

Can you confirm which export you used to generate the report you sent on Friday, and whether Redwood applied any deduping rules or session-timeout windows that might drop late conversions? If there’s a canonical mapping you want us to use for reconciliation, let us know. We’re on a tight close schedule.

Appreciate any logs or a short reconciliation table.

Best,
Sophie Liu
Partnerships, Acme Marketing

--
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Liu <sophie@acmemarketing.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Aaron Ng <aaron@brightwebinars.io>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in webcast lead counts / revenue attribution

Hi Sophie — thanks for flagging this.

Short answer: we rolled together two sources to produce the Friday summary. I should have been clearer — the Friday sheet combined: (1) the Redwood ingestion export (session_id keyed) with a 24h post-session attribution window, and (2) the BrightWebinar lead dump (email keyed) where we attempted a best-effort de-dupe by email. That combination explains some of the mismatches.

Action plan:
- Ben, can you pull the raw ingestion logs (session-level JSON) and export a strict email-keyed list with timestamps for Jul 2–4? Include the original session_id and any redirect parameters. Mark any records where email was inferred or normalized.
- Laura, can you compare that against the HubSpot export Sophie shared and produce a 3-way reconcile with a single canonical "reconciled_email" column and a match_reason field (exact email / redirect param / inferred)?

Sophie — if you can forward the HubSpot CSV and BrightWebinar raw export (or share Drive link), we’ll slot that into the reconciliation.

I’ll aim to have a preliminary table by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Irene
Director, Field Marketing
Redwood Inference

--
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Sophie Liu <sophie@acmemarketing.com>, Aaron Ng <aaron@brightwebinars.io>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in webcast lead counts / revenue attribution

I pulled the ingestion logs and ran the email-key reconciliation you asked for. High-level findings attached (lead_report_20260705.csv). TL;DR:

- Redwood ingestion had 38 distinct emails captured across sessions; 3 of those were inferred from redirect params (no explicit email submitted).
- BrightWebinar export contains 28 explicit registrations with emails. 5 of those map to the same email across multiple session_ids.
- HubSpot export (Sophie’s file) shows 42 contacts created in the campaign window — but 7 of those appear to be manual adds or imports with no session_id or utm_source.

I included a match_reason column (exact / session-redirect / manual-import). The reconciled set using conservative rules (require either exact email OR session_id+redirect) yields 35 unique attributable leads.

Notes on revenue delta: the extra 7 HubSpot contacts include three late-conversion orders that came from an internal import (order IDs noted in the sheet). If Acme chooses to treat manual imports as campaign-attributable, the revenue number moves up by $42k. If you constrain to session-tracked conversions only, the number stays lower.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Agree on canonical rule set for this campaign (we should document for future events): session-first, then explicit email, exclude manual imports unless a confirmed order id maps.
2) If Acme needs to include manual-imports, issue a credit note for the difference in the billed pipeline uplift (we can draft language).
3) Set up a daily HS->Redwood import check for future events to prevent drift.

Attachment: lead_report_20260705.csv (CSV, 540KB) — contains raw rows and the reconciled list with match reasons and revenue tags.

- Ben
Sr. Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

--
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Liu <sophie@acmemarketing.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in webcast lead counts / revenue attribution — Proposed resolution

Hi Sophie — looping back with a proposed resolution so we can close the loop before your end-of-month close.

Summary: Ben’s conservative reconciliation yields 35 attributable leads. HubSpot’s 42 includes 7 manual-import contacts; 3 of those have confirmed orders (Order IDs in Ben’s sheet).

Proposal:
- Redwood will accept the conservative attribution (session-first) as the canonical number for Redwood-sourced pipeline for this hosted webcast.
- For the three confirmed orders that were manual-imported, Redwood will issue a one-time credit equivalent to the agreed event uplift fee on those deals. We’ll send a draft credit note for Acme’s review (DocuSign link will be provided).
- We’ll document the canonical reconciliation rules and add a short checklist for next events: (1) enable session id passthrough on registration redirects, (2) export daily HubSpot sync for 72 hours post-event, (3) avoid manual imports into the campaign bucket without order links.

If that sounds reasonable, Sophie, we’ll attach the draft credit note and final reconciled CSV and route the credit through Finance.

Thanks,
Laura
Sr. Field Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

--
From: Sophie Liu <sophie@acmemarketing.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Aaron Ng <aaron@brightwebinars.io>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in webcast lead counts / revenue attribution — Proposed resolution

Thanks Laura — this is clear and fair.

We accept the session-first canonical number. Please send the draft credit note and the final reconciled CSV; I’ll route for sign-off on our side and confirm once Finance has processed. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sophie
Partnerships, Acme Marketing

Attachments referenced: lead_report_20260705.csv, acme_credit_note_20260706.pdf
